title: Give Ticketly a skeleton
prompt:
Ticketly's home page is built from anonymous divs, and its headings were chosen for their font size. Restructure the markup without changing the text:

- Wrap the logo and the menu in a `<header>`, and make the menu a `<nav>` (give it a name such as `aria-label="Site"`).
- Put the festival content in a single `<main>`.
- Make the copyright line a `<footer>` outside `main`.
- Turn "Harbour Lights 2026" into the only `<h1>`, and fix the other headings so the outline has no skipped levels: Line-up and Tickets are sections; the two passes belong under Tickets.
hints: You can keep the existing class names on the new elements, so the CSS still applies.
Line-up and Tickets sit directly under the h1, so they are h2. The passes sit under Tickets.
header > nav, then main > h1, h2, h2, h3, h3, then footer.
explanation: Landmark elements cost nothing visually but give screen reader users a map: header (banner), nav (navigation), main and footer (contentinfo). The heading levels now describe nesting rather than size: one h1 for the page, h2 for its two sections, and h3 for the passes inside Tickets. The CSS keeps the passes small, because size is a styling decision. Navigating by headings now reads like a table of contents: Harbour Lights 2026, Line-up, Tickets, Friday pass, Weekend pass.

checks.one-main: There is exactly one main landmark holding the festival content
checks.banner-nav: A top-level header contains a nav with the menu links
checks.footer: A top-level footer contains the Terms link
checks.one-h1: "Harbour Lights 2026" is the page's only h1
checks.heading-order: Headings start at h1 and never skip a level; the passes sit one level under Tickets
